This page accompanies the manuscripts, data and interactive atlas. It records what the prepublication review checked, what it corrected, and where independent verification is still needed.

AI-generated research · independent verification pending

The results, proofs, code and data have not yet been independently verified by human experts or formalized in Lean. Treat them as provisional. Automated checks and separate AI reviews establish only their stated scope.

“Realized,” “excluded” and “complete” describe the project’s recorded claims. They do not certify that a proof has received human or proof-assistant verification.

What the review covers

The review examines mathematical hypotheses and cited results separately from tensor calculations, finite certificates, source hashes and the publication interface. A fresh computation can verify an identity; it cannot by itself establish the categorical argument that makes the identity relevant.

The detailed review and reproduction record gives the exact scope and dated corrections. Original research snapshots remain available with their original hashes.

A case has been reopened

The review found an unproved step in the claimed exclusion of R8_2_24. Its proposed repair remains conditional. The current continuation accepts 35 of the original 38 cases, leaving R6_4_155, R6_8_1660 and R8_2_24 open.

Rank eight now records 895 exclusions, 77 models and one open case through multiplicity two. Its complete contiguous range ends at multiplicity one. The dated correction supersedes the older complete-through-two claim.

Corrections to read beside the papers

Rank three · the induced tensor unit

In the near-group proposition, the formula immediately before eq:near-I1 needs three copies of the tensor unit:

(F ∘ I)(1) = 3·1 ⊕ Y ⊕ mX.

The subsequent argument already uses this correct multiplicity. The same proposition’s reference to the moment formula should point to eq:moments in Section 4.

Rank six · two cross-references

The tensor-functor and dimension-block chapters mistakenly cite the Galois-reduction proposition for R6_3_215. For R6_4_155, use prop:nonselfdual-neargroup-spherical; for R6_8_1660, use the unrestricted sphericalization reduction at the start of subsec:frontier-1660 and its published certificate. The detailed review provides exact replacement text.

Both rank-six categorification questions remain open. A compatible necessary-condition witness does not construct a fusion category.

Rank eight · a categorical proof gap

The claimed decorated-phase cancellation in the R8_2_24 proof uses the wrong incoming index. A replacement retaining eight coefficient slots gives the desired algebraic identities, but its categorical transport across an oriented invertible-object crossing has not been proved. The arithmetic does not justify a general exclusion.

The case is therefore reopened. The original proof and its receipts remain historical records; the conditional repair is retained for further investigation. The detailed review distinguishes this retraction from the editorial corrections above.

Reproduction · current versus historical commands

The current historical dispatcher requires the explicit --historical flag. Older bundled READMEs and entry points describe earlier stages; they are not complete fresh checks of all current certificates. Read the current verification guide and the separate full-replay record.

The portable rank-six fermion command, run from the repository root, is:

python evidence/unified_20261016/rank6/verify_fermion_crossing.py --repo .

Rank six · a reproducibility correction

The complete campaign covers all 25,362 exclusion certificates. Seven failed initially because the algebra backend changed the order or orientation of exact equations; all seven then passed their complete unchanged checks under the Python backend. The failed run remains in the record. Separate final checks and a hash-bound coverage audit also passed.

This is a combined campaign, not a successful single full run. The replay packet preserves the original failures, exact comparisons, successful follow-ups and environment limitations. Its new portable orchestrator has not itself been run end to end.

Independent review is still needed

The most delicate arguments concern categorical coherence, simultaneous diagram conventions, sphericalization and conductor-equality refinements. Passing arithmetic checks is not a substitute for establishing those steps. The detailed report identifies specific expert-review priorities and any remaining limits.

If you find an error, a repository issue naming the ring, theorem and precise failing step will make the correction traceable.
